transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thanks for seeing me. 

Um, the main reason I’m here is that anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. In my job, I have to do things like monthly reports or plan multi-site health events, and I just keep putting them off. I know it matters, and I know I need to get it done, but I just avoid it as long as I possibly can. It's really starting to become a problem.

Thinking back, would you say you've struggled with this kind of task avoidance and difficulty focusing since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently, say in the last several months?

No, it's definitely not a recent thing. It's been going on since I was a kid. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but that I was always daydreaming. I was constantly losing my worksheets, and I'd forget to turn in my homework all the time. Honestly, the only way my assignments ever made it to the teacher was because my mother checked my backpack every single night. So, yeah, it's been a lifelong thing.
Growing up, did you also struggle with things like feeling restless, fidgeting, blurting out answers, or having trouble staying seated when you were supposed to?

No, not really. I never really had that problem. I wasn't the type of kid to bounce off the walls or run around the classroom. I could stay in my seat just fine... it was more that my mind was wandering off, not my body. So, no, I didn't struggle with blurting things out or feeling restless like that.
Does this difficulty focusing and finishing tasks show up in other areas of your life too, like at home or in your personal relationships, not just at work?

Yeah, it does. I mean, I’m still getting by overall—both at work and out in the community—but it's definitely taking a toll. 

People have had to step in and cover gaps for me when I drop the ball, and... well, deadlines have slipped. And it spills over into my personal life, too. I’ve really embarrassed myself more than a few times lately with all these last-minute apologies I have to make to coworkers and friends because I forgot something important or just didn't follow through. So, yeah, it's definitely everywhere, not just at the office.
Do you often lose things you need for daily tasks, like your keys, wallet, or phone, or forget routine things like appointments or errands?

Yeah, the forgetfulness is definitely a problem. I don't necessarily lose my physical items like my keys or wallet too often, but routine things... yeah. 

For example, I've been forgetting to return calls from our volunteers. And I'll end up missing small errands I was supposed to run for upcoming events. It's frustrating. Once or twice lately, I’ve even had to apologize because a community meeting just completely slipped my mind until someone texted me to ask where I was. So, yeah, remembering those kinds of daily tasks is definitely a struggle.
Would you say you often struggle to keep your tasks, workspace, or schedule organized—like things becoming messy or disorganized, or having trouble sequencing multi-step projects?

Yeah, definitely. Especially when it comes to keeping my tasks and schedule straight. When I’m juggling work projects, the memorial committee stuff I help with, and various outreach events, it gets pretty messy. I'll end up with my notes in three different places, and... well, I just can’t seem to figure out what needs to happen first. Because I have trouble putting the steps in the right order, I almost always end up rushing at the very end to get it all done.

Over the past several months, have you noticed any persistent low mood, loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, or ongoing feelings of anxiety or worry that might be affecting your concentration?

No, not really. I mean, I'm frustrated with myself for dropping the ball so much lately, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down all the time. And I still care about the things I do, especially the community work. It's just hard to keep it all straight. As for anxiety... I get stressed when I'm running behind or have to apologize again, but I don't feel like I have this constant worry hanging over me that's causing the distraction. It's more like the distraction is causing the stress.

Have you noticed any problems with your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling excessively tired during the day—or do you use alcohol, caffeine, or other substances heavily that might be affecting your concentration?

No, my sleep is actually pretty normal. I don't have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, and I feel fine during the day—not overly tired or anything. And as far as substances go, no. I mean, I drink a regular amount of coffee, maybe a cup or two in the morning, but nothing heavy. I don't really drink alcohol much either, so I don't think any of that is playing a role in my concentration issues.
